checklist_assessment.assessment: Three selectable spirits can be summoned for two Aether, receive levels, and be replaced by a new selection. Selection and resource cost work, but there is no cooldown or meaningful summon failure beyond insufficient Aether.

reason: This is a strong SkiFree-style browser game: the canvas scene has responsive inertia steering, a delta-time requestAnimationFrame loop, scrolling randomized trees/rocks/flags, collisions, particle snow and impact effects, progressive speed, distance, restart, and persistent best-score handling. t0 clearly introduces the controls, while t1 and t2 show the skier progressing through changed terrain as distance rises to about 10 and 20, giving good visible evidence of live motion. checklist_assessment.assessment: The skier has inertia-based steering, scrolling trees/rocks, flags, AABB collisions, distance, penalty/reward logic, and restart. Canvas-drawn skier, trees, rocks, snow texture, flags, particles, and retro typography form a convincing SkiFree-style scene. Assets are simple but coherent and readable at speed.

All features support the downhill game, and effects are restrained. Per-frame localStorage writes are redundant work but do not dominate the presentation.

The crisp blue-and-white pixel presentation, readable HUD, start overlay, and varied obstacles look polished and faithful to the requested retro style. The fixed-size layout is the main presentation limitation.

t0 shows a clear start overlay, while t1 and t2 show the skier moving through different terrain with distance increasing from 0 to about 10 and 20. Motion feedback is convincing, but score remains 00000 in both active frames, visibly confirming the scoring defect.
